title: Trigger-event SOP: decision tree to reopen BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

trigger.note: Set t0 (YYYY-MM-DD) when Gate 1 passes; set final_domestic_decision when the last domestic court decides. Clocks stay on standby while null.

anchors.S7: date the letter before action is sent
anchors.decision: date of that court or body decision
anchors.final_domestic_decision: date of the last domestic decision
anchors.knowledge: date the decisive fact became known

echr_1989.title: William Buckler v the United Kingdom

not_related.title: Buckley v the United Kingdom (Gypsy caravan site, Willingham)

nodes.label: Trigger confirmed
nodes.text: A record shows dishonesty in the 1986–87 evidence, concealment of a record, or government involvement. The date it is first seen is the discovery date (T0). Every clock below counts from T0 or from a later court decision.

deadline.rule: T0 = the date the record is first seen, logged in the custody log

nodes.label: Dishonest evidence in 1986–87
nodes.text: Evidence given, a statement made or a matter concealed in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler was knowingly untrue.

nodes.label: Concealed record
nodes.text: A record relevant to the title or the trial was held back, destroyed or altered.

nodes.label: Government involvement
nodes.text: A public body or official acted in the dispossession, the registration or the handling of the site.

nodes.label: Log the discovery
nodes.text: Custody log entry: date and time seen, who saw it, where (URL, archive reference, letter), how it was obtained. This entry fixes T0.

nodes.label: Preserve and hash
nodes.text: Download the original; sha256 it; Internet Archive Save Page Now for any web page; wayback.bucklerfamily.estate item; R2 copy; offline copy; hash recorded in the custody log; three copies in three places.

nodes.label: Independent check
nodes.text: A second reader checks the record against its source; ask the holder for an official or certified copy; compare with records already held; write the result into the custody log.

nodes.label: Gate 1: record verified?
nodes.text: Is the record genuine, from its stated source, and does it show what it appears to show?

nodes.label: Not verified: log and keep watching
nodes.text: Kept on file; the reopen-loop keeps scoring it; no outside step.

nodes.label: Preservation notice
nodes.text: Short letter to the body holding related records: list the records, ask that they be kept unaltered pending legal advice. Facts only, no accusation.

nodes.label: Instruct a lawyer
nodes.text: Public access barrister (Bar Standards Board directory), solicitor (Law Society Find a Solicitor), Advocate (the Bar Pro Bono Unit), Law Centres Network, Cardiff University pro bono clinics. Send the evidence pack and the custody log.

deadline.rule: opinion requested within 28 days of T0 (target)

nodes.label: Log in HubSpot
nodes.text: One HubSpot task per step with its due date; one note per document; the PRINCE2 Issue Register gets an issue for the trigger.

nodes.label: Gate 2: legal opinion
nodes.text: Written opinion: which test is met, which route, which deadline.

nodes.label: Opinion: no route meets its test
nodes.text: Record the reasons; keep the evidence; the reopen-loop and FOI routes continue.

nodes.label: Letter before action
nodes.text: Drafted with the lawyer under the Practice Direction on Pre-Action Conduct: the facts, what is sought, a reply period.

deadline.rule: reply period: 14 days (straightforward) to 3 months (very complex), PD Pre-Action Conduct para 6(b)

nodes.label: Report to the authorities
nodes.text: Where the opinion points to a crime or a public-body failure: South Wales Police or Action Fraud; IOPC for police conduct; Public Services Ombudsman for Wales; ICO for records destroyed after a request (FOIA s.77); the constituency MP and Member of the Senedd.

deadline.rule: after Gate 2; PSOW within 1 year of notice

nodes.label: Press plan
nodes.text: Only after the letter before action or the report: one factual release citing the documents; officials by role; no private individuals named.

nodes.label: Gate 3: route chosen
nodes.text: The Executive approves the route the opinion recommends; the side project moves to filing.

nodes.label: A. Reopen the 1987 appeal (CPR 52.30)
nodes.text: Court of Appeal will not reopen unless (a) necessary to avoid real injustice, (b) the circumstances are exceptional, (c) there is no alternative effective remedy. Permission needed; decided on paper; no appeal from the decision. Taylor v Lawrence [2002] EWCA Civ 90.

deadline.rule: no fixed limit in the rule; apply promptly after discovery

nodes.decider: Court of Appeal (single judge on permission)

nodes.label: Permission refused (final)
nodes.text: CPR 52.30(7): no appeal or review. Usually not a new Strasbourg start date (Moreira Ferreira v Portugal (no. 2) §60).

nodes.label: Appeal reopened and reheard
nodes.text: The Court of Appeal reconsiders the 1987 appeal.

nodes.label: B. Set aside for fraud (Takhar)
nodes.text: Fresh claim in the High Court. Test (RBS v Highland para 106, adopted in Takhar para 56): conscious and deliberate dishonesty in evidence, a statement or a matter concealed; material, an operative cause of the court’s decision. Takhar para 57: no need to show it could not have been found with reasonable diligence before the trial.

deadline.rule: no fixed limit set by Takhar; issue promptly; linked money or land claims run from discovery under s.32

nodes.decider: High Court (Business and Property Courts in Wales, Cardiff)

nodes.label: Claim dismissed
nodes.text: Appeal to the Court of Appeal with permission; the final decision then starts the Strasbourg clock (C1).

deadline.rule: appellant’s notice 21 days from the decision (CPR 52.12)

nodes.label: 1987 judgment set aside
nodes.text: The possession claim is retried on honest evidence; title and loss follow.

nodes.label: C1. New Strasbourg application
nodes.text: Against the United Kingdom only. Exhaust domestic routes first, then lodge a completed form within four months of the final domestic decision (Art 35(1), four months since 1 Feb 2022). Must carry relevant new information beyond Application 14464/88 (Art 35(2)(b)).

deadline.rule: 4 months from the final domestic decision

nodes.label: C2. Restore Application 14464/88
nodes.text: No route: 14464/88 was declared inadmissible on 14 April 1989; restoration under Art 37(2) and Rule 43(5) covers only struck-out applications.

nodes.label: C3. Rule 80 revision
nodes.text: Revision is for a judgment of the Court, within six months of learning a decisive new fact. 14464/88 ended with a Commission decision, not a Court judgment, so Rule 80 does not reach it. It applies to any future Strasbourg judgment.

deadline.rule: 6 months from learning the fact (future judgments only)

nodes.label: Strasbourg judgment
nodes.text: Finding against the United Kingdom; just satisfaction; Committee of Ministers supervises execution.

nodes.label: D. Limitation Act s.32: claims from discovery
nodes.text: Where the action is based on the defendant’s fraud, or a relevant fact was deliberately concealed, the limitation period starts at discovery (or when it could with reasonable diligence have been discovered). Then 6 years for tort or contract (s.2, s.5) and 12 years for recovery of land (s.15).

nodes.label: Innocent purchaser bar
nodes.text: s.32(3)–(4): no recovery of the property from a purchaser for value since the event who was not a party and had no reason to know. Money claims against those responsible remain.

nodes.label: E. Criminal report
nodes.text: South Wales Police or Action Fraud; the CPS decides charges on a police file; private prosecution is preserved by Prosecution of Offences Act 1985 s.6.

deadline.rule: indictable offences: no time limit; summary-only: 6 months from the offence (MCA 1980 s.127)

nodes.label: No further action
nodes.text: Ask for the reasons and a Victims’ Right to Review where it applies; private prosecution remains (s.6).

nodes.label: F. Judicial review of a new decision
nodes.text: For a decision a public body takes now (a refusal, a registration, a planning step): claim form promptly and in any event within 3 months of the grounds arising; 6 weeks for planning decisions.

deadline.rule: promptly and within 3 months (CPR 54.5(1)); planning 6 weeks (54.5(5))

nodes.label: G. Ombudsman
nodes.text: Public Services Ombudsman for Wales for a Welsh public body; usually after the body’s own complaints process.

deadline.rule: within 1 year of first notice (PSOW Act 2019 s.8(1)(c))
